column23: Calibrated against LYSO. The text assumes LYSO = 33,000 ph/MeV (p.120) but the paper's own Table I lists LYSO = 32,000 ph/MeV -- a 3 percent internal inconsistency in the reference the measurement depends on. The same Table I lists BGO at 8,000 ph/MeV. Samples were cut from the ingot; no surface preparation is described. Shaping time is said to be varied and 'listed in Table I', but Table I contains no shaping time.

column23: Two different 'light yields' in one paper, measured in two different configurations. This row is the radioluminescence value: light taken at 90 degrees through a quartz fibre, so wrapping and coupling are not described (and matter less). The same paper separately reports a photoelectron yield of 21.2 (undoped) and 23.8 (Cu) phe/MeV from a quite different setup -- 1 cm thick crystal, 2-inch PMT at each end, OKEN6262 silicone grease, aluminium foil wrap, 1.1 us gate. Surface is 'polished to the optical grade on the whole surface or on the four of six planes'; which sample got which is not said. Reference BGO is assumed at ~6000 ph/MeV, against 8000 in arXiv:1607.05486, 8500 in Roberts et al. and 10000 in Bonesini.
